'''Abe no Yasuchika''' (安倍泰親) was a {{ill|Nobility|ab|Аамсҭара|af|Adel|als|Adel|ar|نبل|ast|Nobleza|az|Zadəganlıq|ba|Дворянлыҡ|be|Знаць|be_x_old|Дваранства|bg|Аристокрация|bjn|Kasuma|br|Noblañs|bs|Plemstvo|ca|Noblesa|ckb|نەجیبزادەیی|cs|Šlechta|cv|Тăрăн|da|Adel|de|Adel|el|Ευγενείς|eo|Nobelaro|es|Nobleza|et|Aadel|eu|Noblezia|fa|نجیب‌زادگی|fi|Aateli|fr|Noblesse|frr|Aadel|fy|Eallju|ga|Uaisleacht|gan|貴族|gl|Nobreza|he|אצולה|hi|कुलीनवर्ग|hr|Plemstvo|hu|Nemesség|hy|Ազնվականություն|ia|Nobilitate|id|Bangsawan|ig|Onye isi|inh|Эздий|io|Nobeleso|is|Aðall|it|Nobiltà|ja|貴族|jv|Ningrat|ka|თავადაზნაურობა|ko|귀족|ku|Torinî|la|Nobilitas|lb|Adel|lmo|Nobiltà|lt|Diduomenė|lv|Dižciltīgie|min|Bangsawan|mk|Благородништво|mr|सामंतशाही|ms|Golongan bangsawan|myv|Мастачей|mzn|نوبرس|nds_nl|Adel|ne|भारदार परिवार|nl|Adel|nn|Adel|no|Adel|oc|Noblesa|pa|ਕੁਲੀਨਵਰਗ|pl|Szlachta|ps|اشرافیت / اشرافي خلک|pt|Nobreza|ro|Nobilime|ru|Дворянство|sh|Plemstvo|simple|Nobility|sk|Šľachta|sl|Plemstvo|sq|Fisnikëria|sr|Племство|sv|Adel|th|ชนชั้นขุนนาง|tl|Hadlika|tr|Asil|tt|Дворяннар|uk|Шляхта|uz|Dvoryanlar|vec|Nobiltà|vi|Giới quý tộc|wuu|贵族|za|Gveicuz|zh|貴族|zh_min_nan|Kùi-cho̍k|zh_yue|貴族|qid=Q134737|lt=noble}} and {{ill|Onmyōji|en|Onmyōji|qid=Q2274163|lt=onmyōji}} in the late {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}. He served as {{ill|Onmyō no Kami|ja|陰陽頭}} and was a descendant of the famed onmyōji {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|Abe no Seimei|qid=Q1150151|lt=Abe no Seimei}} (five generations removed). His Rank was Shōshiinoge ([[Senior Fourth Rank]], Lower Grade), and he also held the title of {{ill|Dazai Gon no Daibu|ja|大膳権大夫}}.<ref>Concise Japanese Biographical Dictionary, 5th Edition, Sanseido, 2009, p.48.</ref>
== Career ==
=== Succession to the Abe Clan Leadership ===
Yasuchika's father, {{ill|Abe no Yasunaga|ja|安倍泰長}}, served as [[Onmyō no Kami]] with the Rank of [[Junior Fourth Rank|Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade]] until his death in [[:en:Hoan|Hoan]] 2 (1121). Yasuchika’s elder brother, {{ill|Abe no Masafumi|ja|安倍政文|qid=Q140445972}}, succeeded their father but died unexpectedly in {{ill|Tenji|en|Tenji|qid=Q3518096|lt=Tenji}} 1 (1124), leaving the Abe family leadership in jeopardy. As a result, the {{ill|Royal court|en|Royal court|qid=Q1134237|lt=Imperial Court (Japan)}} selected the 15-year-old Yasuchika to lead the clan. His cousin {{ill|Abe no Kintoki|ja|安倍兼時|qid=Q140445981}} became his guardian and teacher in [[Onmyōdō]].<ref>''{{ill|I'in Keizu|ja|医陰系図}}''</ref>
In {{ill|Daiji|en|Daiji|qid=Q5209140|lt=Daiji}} 5 (1130), Yasuchika became {{ill|Right Capital Ward Officer|ja|右京亮}} and soon gained favor with {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽上皇|ja_comment=former now fixed redirect|3=鳥羽天皇|ja_comment=former now fixed redirect|3=鳥羽天皇|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q349284}} and {{ill|Fujiwara no Nariko|en|Fujiwara no Nariko|qid=Q5507535|lt=Empress Bifukumon'in}}. His growing influence led to a legal dispute over the Abe family estate, including the historic {{ill|Tsuchimikado-dono|ja|土御門邸|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135491358}}.<ref>''{{ill|Chūyūki|ja|中右記}}'' and ''{{ill|Minamoto no Morotoki's Diary|ja|長秋記|lt=Nagai Akimitsu's Diary}}'' (entries for 1131).</ref> Yasuchika eventually reclaimed the estate after a prolonged confrontation with his former guardian Kintoki.
=== Rise to Fame as "Sasu no Miko" ===
Yasuchika excelled in [[Onmyōdō]], providing astrological guidance to {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|後白河法皇|ja_comment=former now fixed redirect|3=後白河天皇|ja_comment=former now fixed redirect|3=後白河天皇|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q317984}}. His accurate predictions earned him the title {{nihongo|''Sasu no Miko''|指御子}}, signifying divine insight. He foretold significant events, including the [[1179 political shift|1179 coup]] and the {{ill|Genpei War|ja|治承の乱|ja_comment=former now fixed redirect|3=治承・寿永の乱|ja_comment=former now fixed redirect|3=治承・寿永の乱|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q737542}}.<ref>''{{ill|Taiheiki|ja|台記}}'' (entries for 1148 and 1179).</ref>
His expertise extended to the {{nihongo|''Tensō''|天文奏}}, confidential reports on celestial phenomena. Portions of his journal, ''Abe no Yasuchika no Nikki'', survive today, offering insights into Heian-era {{ill|Astrology|en|Astrology|qid=Q34362|lt=Astrology}}.
== After Yasuchika's Death ==
Following Yasuchika’s death in {{ill|Juei|en|Juei|qid=Q598057|lt=Juei}} 2 (1183), his sons {{ill|Abe no Kiyohiro|ja|安倍季弘|qid=Q140445973}} and {{ill|Abe no Gyōshun|ja|安倍業俊|qid=Q140445974}} continued his legacy. However, internal divisions weakened the Abe clan. It was not until the {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}} that Yasuchika's descendants reestablished the family's prominence.<ref>''{{ill|Meigetsuki|ja|明月記}}'' (entry for 1230).</ref>
